newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban repeat amnesty offer to Afghan opposition.
newsitem.headline: Taleban repeat amnesty offer to Afghan opposition.

text.p: The head of Afghanistan's Taleban interim ruling council repeated an offer of amnesty to opposition fighters on Monday and said that he hoped they would take advantage of it on the Moslem New Year on Thursday.
The offer of amnesty was originally made by Taleban leader Mullah Mohammed Omar, called Amir al-Momineen (Leader of the Faithful) by his followers.

"I call on all opposition fighters to take advantage of the amnesty previously offered by Amir al-Momineen on the occasion of the New Year," head of the Taleban ruling council Mullah Mohammed Rabbani told a conference in Kabul on Monday.

The Taleban, who captured Kabul in September and now control more than 75 percent of Afghanistan, face opposition forces in the snow-bound mountains to the north of Kabul and in the remote northwestern provinces.
There has been little change in the front line over the last month, although there have been reports of heavy fighting in the northwest.
Omar has said that opposition fighters who surrender to the Taleban will be forgiven and allowed to go home.

However, Rabbani has been less forgiving when asked if the amnesty also included opposition leaders such as General Abdul Rashid Dostum and Ahmed Shah Masood, commander of the former government troops.

"This question can be raised when they surrender and repent of their former deeds. Then whatever decision is made by the nation based on Islamic principles will be implemented." he told Reuters in an interview last month.
The Taleban revolutionised Afghan warfare when they offered opposition fighters a choice of disarming and going home or joining the ranks of the Taleban.
In the past the warring factions had ransomed captured opposition fighters and looted their property.

The combination of an offer of humane treatment and the reputation of invincibility has meant that until they encountered the forces of the ex-government around Kabul, the Taleban met little military opposition.
